title: CardinalOps - edge cache fallbacks & VPC / on-prem constraints discovery
summary: Initial reliability & incident tolerance discovery focused on on-prem constraints, VPC networking, edge caching and fallback model routing. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for low-latency inference in EU and APAC. Key concerns: KMS integration, audit logs, cross-region failover, and control of tokenization/caching to meet PII retention policies.
topics: model fallback policies and multi-region routing
action_items: Alex Mercer - Share Private deployment spec + KMS integration guide - due 2026-10-20
Priya Shah - Run quick latency estimate for 512-token chat on rtx-a6000 equivalent in eu-west and ap-southeast - due 2026-10-19
Maya Patel - Share CardinalOps current inference qps by endpoint and peak hour window - due 2026-10-18
next_steps: Alex to send Private/VPC architecture doc and security pack
Customer to provide traffic profile and retention rules
Schedule 1:1 SE deep dive (benchmark run) next week
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 2026-10-14 15:00:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CardinalOps - Head of Platform), Derek Huang (CardinalOps - SRE), Lina Torres (CardinalOps - Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed tradeoffs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for CardinalOps' latency-sensitive routing use cases. Focused on how Redwood handles prefix/edge cache, multi-region failover, private KMS/HSM integration, and audit logging.

00:00 Alex M: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex with Redwood. quick intros?
00:10 Maya P: Hi, Maya here. Head of platform at CardinalOps. We run a hybrid infra footprint, some cloud and some air-gapped for specific clients.
00:18 Derek H: Derek, SRE. I'll be owning the benchmark and rollout details.
00:22 Lina T: Lina, security. I'll get into KMS and compliance questions.
00:28 Priya S: Priya, SE on Redwood side — I'll take the deep-dive on runtime behavior and fallback flows.
00:35 Alex M: Great. Goal for today: understand your constraints and success criteria for reliability and incident tolerance, especially around fallback policies and multi-region behavior.

01:02 Maya P: To start, our primary driver is consistent p99 latency under 400ms for chat endpoints in EU and APAC. We also have strict data residency and some customers require on-prem processing. We're evaluating whether Redwood Hosted can meet that or we'd need Dedicated or Private.
01:25 Alex M: Understood. A couple clarifying q's: current qps, typical session length, and how tolerant you are of partial degradation?
01:33 Derek H: Right now avg is about 60 qps per region with peaks to ~400 qps for 2-3 hours. Typical payloads are 250-600 tokens. For partial degradation — we want graceful degradation, i.e., reduced context window or smaller model fallback rather than outright failures.

03:05 Priya S: Okay that maps to a few options — Hosted can do multi-region routing with regional endpoints, but for strict on-prem or air-gapped we recommend Private. Dedicated sits in the middle with reserved capacity and private peering options. For the graceful fallback, we have model-variant routing policies: can route to a quantized lower-cost variant or a smaller architecture if latency spikes or KV cache miss patterns show degraded performance.
03:40 Lina T: On security, for Private we need KMS/HSM integration plus audit logs exported to our SIEM. SOC 2 is table stakes. Can you confirm the audit log granularity?
03:55 Priya S: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM. Audit logs include per-request metadata (timestamps, model version, route taken, decision on fallback). We can tail logs to your SIEM over secure syslog or push to S3 in your VPC.
04:20 Alex M: I also want to highlight prefix and edge caching — Redwood does prefix caching for repeated prefixes and optional KV-level caching; that can cut p99 dramatically but has to be configured to respect PII retention and cache TTLs.

05:02 Maya P: Can you expand on prefix caching? We have multi-tenant prompts and want to avoid cross-tenant leakage.
05:12 Priya S: Yes, prefix caching keys are namespace-aware, and for Private you can disable cross-tenant cache or set per-tenant TTLs. There's also an opt-in encryption layer for cache entries when using customer KMS.

06:00 Derek H: How do fallbacks get decided? Automatic or policy-driven? For example, if eu-west saturates do you pump to ap-southeast or to a smaller model in eu-west?
06:15 Priya S: Great question. Fallbacks are policy-driven. You define a policy with priority list: e.g., same-region smaller-model, same-region quantized variant, cross-region warm standby, or finally, degrade response (shorter context). You can set thresholds on queue latency, GPU utilization, or token cost. There's also an automated tie-breaker that prefers intra-region options to avoid cold starts.

08:00 Alex M: There's a nuance for compliance — if a tenant requires data to remain in EU, cross-region reroute is not allowed. So policy scoping can be per-tenant.
08:18 Maya P: Exactly. We need per-tenant routing restrictions. Is that supported in Hosted?
08:24 Priya S: In Hosted, multi-region routing is available but per-tenant hard locks on geography require either Dedicated with private routing controls or Private. Hosted can do region pinning at the API key level but the stronger network isolation is in Dedicated/Private.

09:12 Lina T: Also auditability of fallback decisions is critical. If a request was re-routed to ap-southeast, we need a trail saying why and who authorized it.
09:24 Priya S: Audit trail includes the policy evaluation trace — which rule fired, metric values, model chosen. That trace is part of the per-request metadata in Private and Dedicated (with longer retention as an add-on).

10:30 Derek H: On latency — you mentioned preferring intra-region fallback to avoid cold starts. How do you handle KV cache warmup when shifting traffic?
10:45 Priya S: We maintain a warm-KV sync for standby replicas in most deployments. For Dedicated there's a near-instant replica warm path; for Private we can set up pre-warmed standby nodes in your VPC. Cross-region cold starts are the main latency penalty, so policy can prefer local smaller models first.

12:05 Alex M: Let's talk SLAs — what do we offer for Hosted vs Dedicated?
12:12 Priya S: Hosted has best-effort SLAs with published latency profiles but not an uptime SLA. Dedicated comes with an SLA for availability and defined p99 latency targets under committed capacity. Private is a deployment model you operate with Redwood control plane — SLA is negotiated (platform support, runbook assistance available).
12:35 Maya P: For our execs, we need a clear mapping: if we commit to Redwood Dedicated, what availability percent and what are penalties?
12:43 Alex M: We'll capture that in the Commercial pack. In short: Dedicated SLAs cover 99.9% availability for the cluster and financial credits for breaches; we'll send formal SLA language.

14:00 Derek H: Are there built-in chaos or chaos-tested failover playbooks? We run regular DR drills and need to ensure failovers don't cause cascading degradation.
14:12 Priya S: Yes, Redwood has canary and staged rollouts, plus a chaos-playbook template that simulates node loss, region loss, and network partitions. We can provide a runbook and work with your SREs during the pilot to run a controlled drill.

16:10 Maya P: One more on costs: if we do intra-region fallback to a smaller model more often, how do we monitor cost impact vs latency benefit?
16:22 Priya S: Console has token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards. You can also tag routes/tenants and see a projected cost delta for model-variant fallback frequency. There's an Optimize recommendation engine that suggests quantization or cached paths when it sees repeated patterns.

18:00 Lina T: On encryption: do you support envelope encryption with customer KMS for both KV cache and request logs?
18:10 Priya S: Yes for Private. For Dedicated we support KMS for model artifacts and logs; KV cache envelope encryption can be enabled but depends on the storage backend in your VPC. Hosted supports customer-managed KMS for certain enterprise plans.

19:30 Derek H: What's the expected lead time for Private on-prem setup? We have air-gapped client clusters and would need a deployed inference runtime.
19:42 Alex M: Typical on-prem Private deployment timeline is 8-12 weeks for standard configs, longer for heavy compliance/integration (HSM, custom network policies). We do a scoping and then a phased rollout: pilot -> validation -> prod.

21:05 Maya P: In terms of model versions and rollouts, can we pin certain tenants to fixed model hashes so they never get auto-upgraded?
21:14 Priya S: Yes, model pinning per-tenant or per-route is supported. Rollouts are configurable — canary, A/B, or manual. You can set fallback policies per pinned group too.

23:00 Derek H: Let's talk observability — do we get per-request traces into Jaeger/OpenTelemetry?
23:10 Priya S: Yes, Redwood can emit per-request tracing spans including routing decisions, kernel selection, and cache hits. For Private/Dedicated you can forward traces to your tracing endpoint; Hosted supports sampling and configurable export.

25:30 Alex M: Quick note — we sometimes mis-transcribe product names in our docs; sorry in advance if you see Redwood runtime spelled funky in the transcript.
25:40 Maya P: (laughs) no worries.

26:10 Maya P: On constraints: some of our clients prohibit any cross-region data copy even transiently. That kills the warm-KV standby idea unless it's strictly encrypted and never leaves the region in plaintext.
26:28 Priya S: Understood. We can do encrypted replication where only ciphertext moves and decryption keys stay in-region under your KMS. For utterly zero-copy we can prefer smaller models locally and reserve burst capacity.

28:00 Derek H: For the pilot, we want a one-week benchmark that includes a simulated region outage and measure p99, error rate, and failover latency. Can Redwood assist in running that?
28:12 Priya S: Absolutely. SE-run benchmark package: load profile, scripts, and measurement dashboards. We'll need traffic profile and any tenant scoping rules.

30:00 Lina T: Compliance checklist — we need SOC 2, ISO 27001, IL4/5? (some clients). Do you have docs?
30:12 Alex M: We'll share the security pack. Private includes more compliance options; for some IL levels we coordinate with our enterprise compliance team.

32:00 Maya P: How are feature flags handled during failover? e.g., do we get consistent behavior if a fallback model doesn't support a new function-calling hook?
32:12 Priya S: Runtime checks will see if the fallback supports the same interfaces; if not, policy can either block the fallback or synthesize a degraded response. We recommend testing functional parity in the pilot to avoid surprises.

34:20 Derek H: Any hard limits on model kernel selection when using quantized runtimes?
34:30 Priya S: Some model architectures have constrained kernel paths when heavily quantized which can affect throughput. Our Optimize team will advise quantization profiles per model and expected perf delta.

36:00 Alex M: Okay let's do a quick recap and next steps.
36:05 Alex M: Action items: we'll send the Private deployment spec and KMS integration notes (Alex). Priya will run latency estimates for your token sizes and peak qps. Maya will share traffic profile and any tenant restrictions. We'll schedule a pilot benchmark + chaos drill next week.

37:10 Maya P: Sounds good. One last ask — can you include estimated cost delta for running warm standby nodes vs cross-region routing?
37:20 Priya S: Yes, we'll include a cost projection in the pilot deck.

38:00 Derek H: timeline — we aim to decide by end of month and start pilot first week of November.
38:10 Alex M: Noted. We'll move fast on the docs.

39:00 Lina T: I'll also need an NDA addendum for specific client controls; I'll send notes to legal.
39:10 Alex M: Please do — we'll route to our legal.

40:00 (brief hold / background noise)
41:20 Alex M: Thanks everyone, great discussion. Priya, you'll follow up on the latency numbers?
41:26 Priya S: Yep I'll send numbers and a short write-up along with a template for the benchmark.
41:40 Maya P: Thanks all.
41:44 Derek H: Thanks.
41:46 Lina T: Thanks.
41:48 Alex M: Bye everyone.
